target: no absence of stem PO:0009047. 'Caudex absent' says only that the woody perennial stem base is missing. The aerial flowering stems are present, and 'solid' (PATO:0001736 solid configuration) applies to them correctly.
fix: 'caudex absent' / 'without a caudex' -> no stem absence. PO lists caudex only as a synonym of stem (PO:0009047), so an absence of a caudex must not be grounded to stem. Drop it, or ground it to a caudex class if one is added. The synonym is fine for describing a caudex, not for its absence.
reason: An annual Eriogonum with no caudex still has stems, and the same description gives them. Because caudex is a synonym of the whole stem, its absence was turned into 'stem absent'.

target: cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent (PATO:0000462). The cotyledon statement (PO:0020030, incumbent) is about the seed embryo and does not conflict.
fix: 'Cauline leaves absent' / 'stem leaves absent' -> cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent, never leaf/vascular leaf absent. The modifier 'cauline' (and 'basal'/'radical' -> rosette leaf PO:0000014) must be kept when the bearer is grounded.
reason: This is an acaulescent crucifer with basal leaves only. Only the stem leaves are missing, but the modifier was dropped so all leaves became absent, which then clashes with every leaf-like part, cotyledons included.

target: no annotation. 'Flowers not known' means the flowers have not been collected or described, not that the plant has none. Flower PO:0009046 is not absent.
fix: 'flowers not known / not seen / unknown / not yet described', and the same with fruits or other parts, is a statement about the material, not the plant. Never read it as absence. Add these phrases to the context words as 'no annotation'.
reason: The species has cymes with 1 fruit, so it certainly flowers. The flora only lacks flowering material.

target: 'leafless' describes a particular axis (e.g. flowering branches or the lower stem), so it means no leaves on that axis (cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent on that stem), not a whole plant without leaves. The plant's leaves are present, and 'glabrescent' applies to them.
fix: A bare 'leafless' after an axis word (stem, branch, scape, peduncle, 'below', 'in lower part') describes that axis. Read it as no leaves on that axis, not as whole-plant leaf absence. Use whole-plant leafless (FLOPO_0985035) only when 'leafless' describes the plant or habit ('Leafless shrub', 'Plant leafless').
reason: Zataria are leafy shrublets. A statement on leaf hairs in the same taxon shows the leaves exist, so 'leafless' must refer to part of the shoot (older or flowering branches).

target: no annotation. 'Flowers not seen' means no flowering material was available, not that flowers are absent.
fix: 'flowers not seen / not known / unknown' -> no annotation (a statement about the material, not the plant). Never read as flower PO:0009046 absent.
reason: The species has axillary inflorescences. The author only had fruiting or sterile specimens.

target: different bracts of the fig: no external (lateral) bracts on the fig wall, but the basal bracts at the fig base (bract PO:0009055, orbicular) are present
fix: In Ficus and similar descriptions, 'sans bractées externes / latérales' (without external or lateral bracts) is the absence of one kind of bract only. Keep the qualifier, or drop the statement. It must never become bract PO:0009055 absent when 'bractées basilaires' or 'ostiolaires' (basal or ostiolar bracts) are described.
reason: Fig descriptions separate basal, lateral (external) and ostiolar bracts. The absence concerns lateral bracts only.

target: the dots on the leaf surface are absent (leaf lamina PO:0020039 not punctate PATO:0001512 / not gland-dotted FLOPO:0991174). The leaf is not absent. This is a negated quality, so it may be left unannotated.
fix: 'dots / hairs / glands / papillae / scales absent' is the absence of a surface feature on the part under discussion. Ground it to that feature (or a negated quality), never to the part that bears it. If the feature has no class, drop the statement rather than move the absence to the bearer.
reason: In Myristica the 'dots' are small dots on the leaf underside. The leaves themselves are described at length.
